research_mode: official Home Office primary police-workforce statistics only; scope, counting and comparability methodology gates; no parcel result or local safety score claimed

sources.name: Police-workforce snapshot date
verified_claims: The release describes workers in post on 31 March 2026 and is a point-in-time workforce snapshot.
limitations: A snapshot does not measure staffing throughout the year or deployment at an incident date.

sources.name: Territorial-force coverage
verified_claims: Headline England and Wales totals cover the 43 territorial police forces.
limitations: They do not automatically include British Transport Police or National Crime Agency personnel.

sources.name: BTP and NCA analysis boundary
verified_claims: BTP and NCA figures appear in accompanying tables but are largely excluded from headline analysis and territorial-force totals.
limitations: Adding these figures to headline totals requires explicit scope reconciliation.

sources.name: Full-time-equivalent convention
verified_claims: Workforce figures are presented on a full-time-equivalent basis unless otherwise stated.
limitations: FTE measures capacity and is not identical to the number of individual people.

sources.name: Headcount availability
verified_claims: Accompanying data tables also provide headcount information.
limitations: FTE and headcount values must not be mixed in a single rate without conversion.

sources.name: Long-term-absence inclusion in totals
verified_claims: Unless stated otherwise, total workforce figures include people on career breaks or other long-term absence.
limitations: Total workforce is not the same as personnel currently available for operational deployment.

sources.name: Secondment counting convention
verified_claims: Personnel seconded into a force are included, while those seconded out to central services are excluded from that force's figures.
limitations: Secondment flows can affect force comparisons without representing recruitment or loss from policing overall.

sources.name: OPCC worker exclusion
verified_claims: Workers in or supporting Offices of Police and Crime Commissioners are excluded from force workforce figures.
limitations: These exclusions mean the release is not a total count of every person employed in the wider policing governance system.

sources.name: Frontline-policing model
verified_claims: Functions are mapped through the CIPFA Police Objective Analysis framework into visible operational, non-visible operational, frontline support and business support categories.
limitations: A frontline classification does not prove physical presence in a particular neighbourhood or incident.

sources.name: Function-proportion exclusions
verified_claims: Function proportions exclude records classed as Other, National Policing or unknown function.
limitations: Published proportions do not use every officer as the denominator.

sources.name: Other-function content
verified_claims: The Other function includes specified long-term leave and students still in classroom-based training.
limitations: Other must not be interpreted as an operational specialty.

sources.name: Student-function comparability break
verified_claims: Updated guidance records classroom-based student officers as Other, making functions data from 2025 onwards not directly comparable with earlier years.
limitations: Trend analysis across 2024 and 2025 must preserve this classification break.

sources.name: Special-constable headcount convention
verified_claims: Special constables and police support volunteers are reported by headcount because they do not have contracted working hours.
limitations: Their headcount cannot be added directly to FTE paid-workforce totals as equivalent capacity.

sources.name: Staff and designated-officer combination
verified_claims: Police staff and designated officers are combined because some forces cannot provide them separately.
limitations: The combined series cannot support complete designated-officer-only comparisons.

sources.name: Neighbourhood personnel in training
verified_claims: Neighbourhood Policing Programme totals include officers and PCSOs in training who are destined for neighbourhood roles.
limitations: Destined-for-role personnel are not yet necessarily deployed in neighbourhood policing.

sources.name: Neighbourhood statistics status
verified_claims: The training-destination component is confirmed by forces but not independently reviewed by the OSR and is Official Statistics rather than Accredited Official Statistics.
limitations: It requires the stated quality designation and must not inherit accreditation from other workforce tables.

sources.name: Neighbourhood baseline revision boundary
verified_claims: The programme baseline is fixed as first published and can differ from routinely revised functions open-data figures.
limitations: Baseline and revised-series values must not be silently substituted.

sources.name: Neighbourhood-growth cohort limitation
verified_claims: Neighbourhood growth is a net snapshot increase and does not identify a stable cohort because people join, leave and move functions.
limitations: Characteristics of a specific growth cohort cannot be inferred from the net FTE change.

sources.name: Neighbourhood joiner-role timing boundary
verified_claims: A person recorded in neighbourhood policing at year end may have joined another function and transferred during the year.
limitations: Year-end function does not establish the function at recruitment.

sources.name: Length-of-service recording quality
verified_claims: Some forces record length of service from the current-role start rather than police-service start, which can skew values toward shorter service.
limitations: Service-length comparisons require caution and must not be used as exact experience measures without force-specific validation.
